tasks.short: Inspect received products and decide whether to accept, quarantine or reject them.

steps.what: Retrieve receipt details and the applicable inspection checklist.
Inspect packaging, product condition and any required sample functions.
Decide whether to accept, quarantine or reject the products.
Record findings and update the stock disposition.
Send discrepancy details to the purchasing and warehouse teams.

tasks.design: Configure receipt-linked inspection forms in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, using controlled checklists from {DOCS}. The supervisor inspects the goods and confirms disposition; the form saves the inspection record, updates stock status and routes discrepancies through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition is physical and product-specific. Separate receipt screens, checklists and messages made supporting paperwork awkward to connect.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing inspection forms and workflow rules can connect receipt data, structured findings and stock status. AI-assisted coding can reduce the effort of missing connectors without replacing physical judgement.
tasks.still_hard: Hidden defects, specialist testing and disputed acceptance criteria still require expertise. Product categories may need different inspection methods.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising an unusual defect and judging whether it affects safety, saleability or customer expectations.

ambition.what: Review recurring supplier defects monthly using linked inspection records.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time retrieving references and copying findings. Their acceptance authority stays unchanged; recurring defect evidence supports requests for corrective action.

reach.task: Confirm whether available stock is suitable for a customer order.
reach.learn: Read inspection status and understand when a defect limits the intended use.

evidence.claim: Receipt-linked forms and rule-based notifications can reduce inspection administration without automating physical inspection.
General-purpose software cannot establish hidden physical defects without suitable observations or tests.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a supervisor responsible for physical goods and acceptance decisions.
The company records goods receipts in the {OPS_SYSTEM} and maintains inspection criteria.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Consent and access estimates cover permissions and a consultation assessment; any required national process may take longer.
unknowns: Which product categories require specialist inspection or mandatory testing?
Who may release, quarantine or reject stock?
Does the {OPS_SYSTEM} support receipt-linked forms and disposition updates?
Are employee identifiers or photos captured, and do national consultation rules apply?
research_questions: Which existing inspection functions can be configured before building an extension?
Which checklist fields remove duplicate entry without slowing physical inspection?
new_work: Maintain inspection checklists and disposition permissions.
Resolve receipts with missing or conflicting product references.
Check failed stock updates and notification delivery.
Review recurring defects and inconsistent inspection records.

tasks.short: Check product prices, presentation and advertised functions, then arrange corrections.

steps.what: Retrieve approved prices, display instructions and advertised product claims.
Compare displayed prices and presentation with the approved references.
Test demonstrated functions against the advertised product claims.
Decide which discrepancies require correction, withdrawal or specialist investigation.
Correct physical labels and displays, or remove unsuitable demonstration products.
Publish approved price corrections to the customer-facing catalogue.
Record completed corrections and notify the owner of unresolved issues.

tasks.design: A deterministic job combines approved prices from the {ERP} with versioned display instructions and claims from {DOCS}. A mobile form in {WORKFLOW} supports physical checks, prepares replacement labels and routes unresolved findings. Approved catalogue price corrections pass through a validated connector to {ECOMMERCE}, with approval attached to publication.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical presentation and functional checks depend on context. Price references, product claims and correction records often sit apart.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured product identifiers, versioned references and simple forms can connect the administrative work. Deterministic comparisons handle prices where both values are available as data.
tasks.still_hard: Real-world performance tests and misleading presentation remain judgement-heavy. Product identifiers, customer-specific prices and catalogue variants can complicate matching.
tasks.human_edge: Judging whether the presentation or demonstration creates an expectation the product cannot meet.
tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time assembling references and documenting corrections. Physical checks remain a substantial part of the week, and pricing decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Validate a demonstration against technical product claims.
reach.learn: Define repeatable acceptance tests and distinguish a setup fault from a product limitation.

evidence.claim: Structured price comparisons and approved publication flows can use deterministic rules.
Physical presentation and functional testing still require direct observation and product expertise.
Where applicable, EU consumer price-reduction rules require the relevant prior-price reference; business-only pricing needs separate treatment.

assumptions: This task concerns a non-retail sales showroom or demonstration area with an associated customer-facing catalogue.
Approved prices and product claims already exist; the solution does not choose pricing policy.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates, not measured savings.
Consent and access estimates cover permissions and a consultation assessment; any required national process may take longer.
unknowns: Which physical and digital sales surfaces fall within the supervisor's responsibility?
Are prices public, customer-specific or both?
Which product claims have approved test procedures?
Who may approve catalogue changes and product withdrawal?
Do captured photos include people, and are national consultation requirements triggered?
research_questions: Can existing catalogue functions compare published and approved prices?
Which checks need physical testing, and which can use structured product data?
Which consumer pricing rules apply to the actual sales channels?
new_work: Maintain approved price, claim and checklist versions.
Resolve ambiguous product and catalogue matches.
Check connector failures and confirm physical corrections were completed.

tasks.short: Assess territory growth potential and propose fair, achievable sales quotas.

steps.what: Export territory sales, pipeline and account coverage data.
Reconcile territory mappings, periods, currencies and missing account data.
Assess growth, penetration, pipeline quality and account concentration by territory.
Calculate quota scenarios against revenue targets, capacity and territory potential.
Recommend quotas and explain territory-specific adjustments.
Challenge assumptions and approve or revise the quota proposal.
Enter approved quotas and distribute the territory plan.

tasks.design: Scheduled connectors reconcile {CRM} and {ERP} data in the {DATA_PLATFORM} and feed a territory dashboard in {BI}. Deterministic scenario calculations expose assumptions, capacity limits and target totals; the supervisor adds commercial judgement. A recorded sales manager approval releases quota updates to the {CRM} through {WORKFLOW}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Territory mappings and definitions differ between sales and finance. Quota politics and uncertain market potential cannot be settled by a calculation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing data connectors, dashboards and versioned calculation rules make repeatable scenarios practical. AI-assisted coding can shorten development, but data definitions still need agreement.
tasks.still_hard: Market potential is only partly observable. Inherited account quality, vacancies, long sales cycles and quota-linked pay can make apparently equal targets unfair.
tasks.human_edge: Weighing commercial context, explaining trade-offs and negotiating targets that people can defend.

ambition.what: Hold a monthly territory-capacity review between formal quota-setting rounds.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor shifts from assembling quarterly workbooks to investigating territory constraints and preparing monthly capacity options. They gain faster scenario access; the sales manager retains quota approval.

reach.learn: Interpret scenario sensitivity, distinguish potential from pipeline, and assess quota effects on incentives.

reach.task: Prioritise under-covered accounts within a territory.
reach.learn: Use account coverage and potential measures without treating uncertain estimates as facts.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales supports sales-data questions and open-deal risk flags; this does not establish automated quota-setting capability.
Territory reconciliation, quota arithmetic and scenario comparisons can use deterministic code.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; quota decisions require assessment of their actual effects.
If AI is added to employee task allocation or performance evaluation, its intended use must be assessed against the EU AI Act employment provisions.

assumptions: The supervisor proposes quotas and a sales manager approves them.
Territory reporting currently combines {CRM}, {ERP} and spreadsheet work.
The initial design uses no model-based employee scoring or autonomous agent.
Step shares cover the end-to-end task, including approval, and are estimates rather than measured savings.
Consultation and access ranges include employee-data review and national consultation where applicable; statutory or negotiated processes may exceed them.
unknowns: Who owns territory mappings and can reconcile disputed account assignments?
Which market-potential data is licensed and sufficiently reliable?
Do quotas affect contractual pay, bonuses or other significant employment outcomes?
Which national consultation requirements apply to the proposed reporting changes?
Which employee-level data may the supervisor access?
research_questions: Which historical periods can validate the quota calculations without treating past sales as total potential?
What review and challenge process applies when quotas affect pay?
Can current {CRM} and {BI} configuration supply the required scenarios before custom development?
new_work: Resolve territory mapping and data-quality exceptions.
Maintain calculation definitions and versioned scenario assumptions.
Review unusual quota changes and document commercial adjustments.
Monitor access permissions and retain approval records.
Compare scenario assumptions with later outcomes.

tasks.short: Check stock, resolve discrepancies and reorder products at approved thresholds.

steps.what: Check recorded stock, reservations and incoming deliveries.
Count relevant physical stock and note damaged or unavailable units.
Reconcile count differences and approve stock adjustments.
Compare available stock with reorder levels and calculate required quantities.
Enter replenishment quantities and supplier details into a purchase requisition.
Review quantities, spending limits and exceptions before approving the purchase.
Issue the approved purchase order to the supplier.

tasks.design: Configure stock availability and reorder rules in the {OPS_SYSTEM}, including reservations, incoming orders, pack sizes and supplier lead times. Mobile counting records discrepancies, while replenishment proposals flow to the {PROCUREMENT} approval queue. The {PROCUREMENT} issues orders only against recorded approval and prevents duplicate transmission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock accuracy, unreliable lead times and disconnected purchasing records made unattended ordering difficult. Reorder functionality may already exist but be poorly configured.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured inventory and purchasing functions already cover most threshold ordering. Better identifiers and small connectors can remove spreadsheet calculations and requisition re-entry.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock accuracy, shortages, obsolete goods and supplier constraints remain operational problems. Thresholds need maintenance when demand or lead times change.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when an apparent stock shortage reflects damaged goods, a customer commitment or an unreliable supplier.

ambition.what: Review replenishment exceptions daily before customer commitments are put at risk.

tasks.altitude: The supervisor spends less time calculating and entering routine orders and more time resolving availability risks. Purchase approval and stock-adjustment authority remain unchanged.

reach.task: Confirm availability and delivery dates for customer orders.
reach.learn: Distinguish physical stock, reserved stock and unconfirmed incoming supply.

reach.task: Discuss alternatives when a requested product is unavailable.
reach.learn: Read replenishment exceptions and avoid promising unconfirmed delivery dates.

evidence.claim: RELEX Solutions provides forecasting and replenishment; the digest describes a retail deployment moving from manual planning, not a measured result for non-retail supervisors.
Threshold replenishment, purchase approval and order transmission generally fit configured inventory and purchasing software.
Physical counting and unresolved stock discrepancies limit how much of the complete task can be automated.

assumptions: This supplemental task applies to a supervisor responsible for merchandise availability.
The {OPS_SYSTEM} holds stock movements and the {PROCUREMENT} holds supplier and approval records.
A spreadsheet currently bridges stock checks and purchasing; if integrated replenishment is already active, savings are smaller.
Step shares cover all actors and are planning estimates rather than measured savings.
Access estimates include approval permissions and a consultation assessment; national consultation may apply if employee monitoring changes.
unknowns: Are reorder functions already licensed, configured and used?
How accurate are stock balances, reservations and incoming delivery dates?
Which order values or product categories require purchase approval?
Can the systems exchange requisitions without duplicate orders?
Would counting records introduce new employee monitoring under national rules?
research_questions: Can existing replenishment configuration remove the spreadsheet bridge?
Which availability definition prevents over-ordering against open purchase orders?
What checks detect duplicate orders, stale counts and failed transmissions?
new_work: Maintain reorder levels, pack sizes and supplier lead times.
Review stock discrepancies and replenishment exceptions.
Handle failed or duplicate order transmissions.
Check whether repeated overrides indicate poor stock data or outdated rules.

role.altitude: The supervisor retains physical product judgement, commercial interpretation and people-facing quota discussions. Their week contains less reference gathering, reconciliation and re-entry, with more frequent reviews of supplier defects, territory capacity and stock exceptions; approval rights remain with existing authorised roles.
reach: Sales manager: prepare territory capacity options and explain quota trade-offs.
Sales engineer: structure product demonstration tests and interpret limitations.
Order clerk: connect stock exceptions to credible customer delivery commitments.
skills_to_grow: Define reliable product, territory and stock identifiers.
Configure thresholds, exception routes and approval permissions.
Interpret scenario assumptions and uncertain market estimates.
Design practical inspection and demonstration checklists.
Explain quota adjustments and support meaningful challenge.
Maintain employee-data access controls and assess applicable national consultation requirements.
role.ambitious_version: Run a monthly sales-readiness review that connects territory capacity, stock availability and product defects. Bring specific capacity, supplier or availability proposals to the sales manager while preserving human approval of consequential decisions.

job.title: First-Line Supervisors of Non-Retail Sales Workers
